conventions.convention: Tempered distributions are continuous complex-linear functionals; distribution-test pairings are bilinear.

Time reflection is ϑ(t,x)=(-t,x). The positive-time algebra is generated by compactly supported smooth tests in t>0. Θ conjugates coefficients, reflects tests, and reverses products; reflection positivity means ω(Θa a)≥0 on this algebra.

Distributional convergence is tested separately at each fixed order and fixed Schwartz test along a nonempty directed regulator set. Per-order continuity bounds, cross-order growth, and clustering are separate conditions.
The free covariance uses Fourier kernel exp(-ip·x), inverse normalization (2π)^(-d), m>0, and full Axiom of Choice. In dimension one, the spatial factor R^0 has unit mass.
The finite-site reflection exchanges X and Y, and the positive-site algebra is generated by Y; the counterexample parameter satisfies 0<r<1.

load_bearing.statement: Defines dimension-d Schwinger hierarchies, ordinary moment positivity, reflection positivity, fixed-order distributional limits, separate continuity and growth records, Euclidean invariance, permutation symmetry, and clustering. It asserts neither existence nor reconstruction.

For p,q≥1 and tempered distributions u and v, the iterated pairing on Schwartz tests defines a tempered distribution, has the product values, agrees with the distribution tensor product on compactly supported tests, is unique with these product values, and has associative finite iterates.

Reflection positivity passes under fixed-order distributional convergence of hierarchies on the same positive-time algebra. Euclidean invariance and permutation symmetry also pass under the stated fixed test transformations. These hypotheses yield no clustering or order-uniform growth conclusion.

Under the Axiom of Choice, for every integer d≥1 and m>0, the stated massive Euclidean covariance is ordinarily positive and has the displayed reflected Gram factorization. Its Wick pairing hierarchy consists of tempered distributions and has a normalized positive and reflection-positive moment functional. No continuum probability measure or Osterwalder–Schrader reconstruction is asserted.
